rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's denial of ownership means he cannot effect harm or benefit by his own power.
rows.anchor: كما تقدم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm comes first because the audience awaited a threat; harm is easier to cause, so benefit after it is a rhetorical ascent.
rows.anchor: وقدم الضر على النفع لأنه أنسب بالغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning both harm and benefit comprehensively covers the two kinds of conditions.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من جمع الأمرين الإحاطة بجنسي الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected and means “but”: whatever benefits or harms me is only what God wills.
rows.anchor: نفعي وضري هو ما يشاءه الله لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer refutes their challenge by a demonstrative argument: if he cannot control even his own welfare, he cannot bring their promised punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب يقتضي إبطال كلامهم بالأسلوب المصطلح على تلقيبه في فن البديع بالمذهب الكلامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's nearest possible control would concern the self, yet benefits and harms depend on interlinked events beyond human control, so people are directed by God's power.
rows.anchor: الإنسان مسيرا في شؤونه بقدرة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment comes from God, not the Prophet, and has a divinely fixed time.
rows.anchor: الوعد من الله لا مني وأنا لا أقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Every community has a term” explains why he cannot set the punishment: God appoints each community's term wisely, including its punishment.
rows.anchor: الله قدر آجال أحوال الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal premise includes the addressees: they are a community, so they too have a term and should await it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المخاطبون من جملة الأمم كانوا مشمولين لحكم هذه القضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning “when their term comes” describes the term as fixed and unchangeable.
rows.anchor: أي أجل محدود لا يقبل التغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When” carries conditional force, so the following fa marks its clause as the consequence.
rows.anchor: فلذلك اقترنت جملة عاملها بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second answer: even if the requested punishment came, belief would bring no benefit because the punishment would kill them first; the hypothetical concession follows the initial refutation.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب ثان عن قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night/day pair makes the threat vivid and exhaustive, portraying it as imminent whether it comes at night or the next morning.
rows.anchor: هاذين الوقتين لا يخلو حلول الحوادث عن أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “By night” also contrasts a nearer or less-near arrival and summons them to picture the event as an admonition.
rows.anchor: على أن في ذكر هذين الوقتين تخييلا ما لصورة وقوع العذاب استحضارا له لديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayāt is a verbal noun for nighttime attack, like salām for taslīm; it functions adverbially with an implied noun for time.
rows.anchor: اسم مصدر التبييت ، ليلا كالسلام للتسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are God's reply to Pharaoh's profession of faith, understood as a request to escape drowning after acknowledging God's lordship.
rows.anchor: لأنه قصد بقوله ذلك طلب الإنجاء من الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God speaks through the angel assigned to punish Pharaoh to extinguish his hope of salvation in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال الله هذا الكلام له على لسان الملك الموكل بتعذيبه تأييسا له من النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh had recognized Moses' claims and hoped that confessing divine unity would secure rescue; the following verse confirms that context.
rows.anchor: علم أن ما حل به كان بسبب غضب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “Now?” is a rebuke; an omitted verb is “now you believe,” with the time placed first because it is the focus of denial.
rows.anchor: ظرف لفعل محذوف دل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke means faith at the moment of death cannot save its bearer in this world or the next.
rows.anchor: والمنفي هو إيمان ينجي من حصل منه في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time word “now” denotes the present, as in the earlier usage in al-Anfal.
rows.anchor: خفف الله عنكم في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause intensifies the rebuke: Pharaoh had disobeyed, corrupted religion, and spread earthly oppression and deception by magic.
rows.anchor: وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You were among the corrupters” is more emphatic than simply calling him a corrupter; greater wrongdoing brings more severe punishment.
rows.anchor: أبلغ في الوصف بالإفساد من : وكنت مفسدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa introduces an implied condition: if late faith seeks rescue, only the corpse will be saved; calling that rescue is a taunting metaphor.
rows.anchor: فإطلاق الإنجاء على إخراجه من البحر استعارة تهكمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor also rests on resemblance: bringing the intact body ashore looks like rescue while being its opposite.
rows.anchor: لأن إخراجه إلى البر كاملا بشكته يشبه الإنجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ba in “with your body” is most likely emphatic; “body” means a lifeless body and rules out rescue from drowning.
rows.anchor: مزيدة للتأكيد ، أي تأكيد آية إنجاء الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra qualification “your body” is meaningful rather than filler, consistent with the Arabic preference for concise eloquence.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو لم يكن المقصود الاقتصار على تلك الحالة لما كان داع للبليغ أن يزيد ذلك القيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those left behind are later generations, especially Pharaoh's officials and priests; his corpse disproves claims that Pharaoh could not be defeated or had ascended to heaven.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم من يخلفه من الفراعنة ومن معهم من الكهنة والوزراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian beliefs that dead Pharaohs entered an afterlife explain their pyramids and grave goods; drowning while pursuing Israel left no room for that deception.
rows.anchor: فهم مضطرون إلى الاعتراف بأنه غرق إذا نظروا في تلك الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question follows the audience's failure to benefit from signs and warnings: ask what they await, and answer that they await the fate of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: ويجاب بأنهم ما ينتظرون إلا مثل ما حل بمن قبلهم ممن سيقت قصصهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is mockingly reproachful: they are treated as waiting for something to believe, though only the destructive days of earlier peoples remain.
rows.anchor: نزلوا منزلة من ينتظرون شيئا يأتيهم ليؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Days” stands for the great events occurring in them, as in the Arab phrase “the days of the Arabs.”
rows.anchor: وأطلقت الأيام على ما يقع فيها من الأحداث العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Say, then, wait” grows out of the question; inserting “say” emphasizes the shift from God's address to the Prophet to the Prophet's address to his people.
rows.anchor: ولينتقل من مخاطبة الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unusual transition between speakers still forms one communicated message and makes the consequence concise: a threat that also promises the Prophet victory.
rows.anchor: وهذا موقع غريب لفاء التفريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I am with you among those waiting” answers an implied question about the Prophet's own stance and is an indirect way to say he awaits victory.
rows.anchor: ها نحن أولاء ننتظر وأنت ماذا تفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared waiting is only the act of waiting, not the outcome; the Prophet awaits the opposite of what will happen to them.
rows.anchor: فالمعية في أصل الانتظار لا في الحاصل بالانتظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to save the messengers follows the threatened days: God reassures the Prophet and believers that He will save them as He saved earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: عجل الله البشارة للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” is a concluding summary referring back to the deliverance just promised.
rows.anchor: إلى الإنجاء المستفاد من { ثم ننجي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A duty upon Us” is parenthetical and treats deliverance as a graciously honored commitment from God.
rows.anchor: وجعله الله حقا عليه تحقيقا للتفضل به والكرامة حتى صار كالحق عليه

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads the second nun quiescent and the jīm light, from the form inja; the meaning matches the other reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hafs from Asim shares al-Kisa'i's light-jīm reading; other readers use a doubled jīm, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parenthetical warning follows the challenge to submit: if people seek worldly rank instead of truth, their worldly enjoyment ends in lasting punishment; the second clause is the main point.
rows.anchor: من هذا الكلام هو الجملة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning explains resistance to faith and cautions Muslims not to mistake unbelievers' worldly ease for divine approval or assume disbelief brings immediate punishment.
rows.anchor: وفيه تنبيه المسلمين بأن لا يغتروا بظاهر حسن حال الكافرين في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet renounced much luxury and adornment, framing the women choice as a question of lifestyle.
rows.anchor: عن كثير من ذلك الترف وتلك الزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's wives' choice of worldly life means comfort and clothing, not rejecting the afterlife, so it concerns a different sense of worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: فذلك في معنى آخر من معاني الحياة وزينتها وهو ترف العيش وزينة اللباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “to them” refers to the people described by the relative clause.
rows.anchor: الموصولة لأن المراد بها الأقوام الذين اتصفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives their chosen worldly works in full by leaving them free of faith's burdens; believers forgo some enjoyment to obey God and avoid its afterlife consequences.
rows.anchor: إعطاء الشيء وافيا ، أي كاملا غير منقوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “complete” takes ila because it also conveys “deliver” or “bring,” allowing both senses.
rows.anchor: لتضمنه معنى نوصل أو نبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not promise every desire to whoever wants worldly life: it says their works are completed and left to them without the burdens of faith.
rows.anchor: فليس معنى الآية أن من أراد الحياة وزينتها أعطاه الله مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not deprived of worldly blessings as punishment for unbelief; God leaves them to their lot as respite and gradual enticement, showing unbelief does not bar divine blessing.
rows.anchor: لا يجازون على كفرهم بجزاء سلب بعض النعم عنهم بل يتركون وشأنهم استدراجا لهم وإمهالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “in it” may refer either to worldly life or to their works.
rows.anchor: وضمير { فيها } يجوز أن يعود إلى { الحياة } وأن يعود إلى ( الأعمال )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next sentence is independent but linked by “those”; the demonstrative marks the people and signals that their prior traits justify the judgment.
rows.anchor: وأتي باسم الإشارة لتمييزهم بتلك الصفات المذكورة قبل اسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means that nothing in the afterlife is theirs except the Fire, which entails eternal punishment and identifies them as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على الخلود في النار فيدل على أن هؤلاء كفار عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hābiṭ means becoming void or annihilated.
rows.anchor: الحبط : البطلان أي الانعدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What they made” means their deeds, including worldly kindness such as feeding the needy; ṣanīʿa names a benevolent deed, fitting the wording.
rows.anchor: ومن الإحسان من الدنيا كإطعام العفاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In it” may refer to this world, modifying their deeds, or the afterlife, where their deeds have no effect; their share of divine favor is confined to worldly life.
rows.anchor: المتحدث عنها فيتعلق المجرور بفعل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Umar that Persians and Romans had received their good things early in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمر لما ذكر له فارس والروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's call is explained by “My son, board with us”: it is a gentle invitation and guidance.
rows.anchor: وهي إرشاد له ورفق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not be with the disbelievers” explains that refusal to board places the son among them, since it shows disbelief in the flood.
rows.anchor: يجعله في صف الكفار إذ لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Board with us” is an indirect invitation to faith through an offer and warning; the son's mountain claim mocks the warning.
rows.anchor: عن دعوته إلى الإيمان بطريقة العرض والتحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive “my son” expresses tenderness and compassion; its morphology contracts ibn and assimilates the possessive yā.
rows.anchor: وتصغيره هنا تصغير شفقة بحيث يجعل كالصغير في كونه محل الرحمة والشفقة

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads the possessive yā in “my son” with fatḥa in the vocative; the majority leave it with kasra.
rows.anchor: بفتح ياء المتكلم المضاف إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son said this before the flood reached mountain peaks; āwī means to descend or take shelter, and its verbal noun is al-awy.
rows.anchor: قبل أن يبلغ الماء أعالي الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That will protect me from the water” can describe a high mountain or answer an implied question: the son thought the highest peaks would stay dry.
rows.anchor: لأنه استشعر أن نوحا عليه السلام يسأل لماذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No protector exists against God's commanded flood except those whom He mercifully destined to survive; that mercy appeared in revelation of the ark and instructions.
rows.anchor: من قدر الله له النجاة من الغرق برحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is from the implicit object of “protector,” since a protector necessarily implies someone protected.
rows.anchor: إذ العاصم يقتضي معصوما وهو المستثنى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawj names waves or masses of water rising through wind or inflow; the sea's turbulence also gives the word a metaphorical use for an agitated crowd.
rows.anchor: مقادير من ماء البحر أو النهر تتصاعد على سطح الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wave coming between Noah and his son conveys how quickly the flood rose during the attempt to escape.
rows.anchor: وحيلولة الموج بينهما في آخر المحاورة يشير إلى سرعة فيضان الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the son was among the drowned concisely implies that the others Noah warned drowned too.
rows.anchor: أنه غرق وغرق معه من توعده بالغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative moves from the son's drowning to the flood's end.
rows.anchor: وقوع الغرق الموعود به على وجه الإيجاز كما علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive “it was said” omits its obvious speaker, God; the utterance is a creative command.
rows.anchor: مثله لا يصدر إلا من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing earth and sky as listeners is a dependent metaphor for God's creative command affecting their states as if they obeyed willingly.
rows.anchor: وخطاب الأرض والسماء بطريقة النداء وبالأمر استعارة لتعلق أمر التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Swallow” literally means food passing into the throat; here it depicts water quickly entering the earth's interior, perhaps through fissures or subsidence.
rows.anchor: والبلع حقيقته اجتياز الطعام والشراب إلى الحلق بدون استقرار في الفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Its water” is attributed to the earth by loose association because the water lay on its surface.
rows.anchor: لأدنى ملابسة لكونه في وجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's “retiring” means rain stopped; earth-swallowing is named first because the rain was the main source of the excess water.
rows.anchor: وإقلاع السماء مستعار لكف نزول المطر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired earth and sky create antithesis, while “swallow” and “retire” create paronomasia.
rows.anchor: وفي مقابلة ( ابلعي ) ب { أقلعي } محسن الجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The water receded” summarizes both causes; its passive form reflects the resulting process, and the floodwater means water in excess of normal seas and valleys.
rows.anchor: مغن عن التعرض إلى كون السماء أقلعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive “the matter was completed” leaves God as the understood sole agent; completing the matter means bringing it to its end.
rows.anchor: وبناء الفعل للنائب للعلم بأن فاعله ليس غير الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Moses' scripture consoles the Prophet: even people of scripture, in a better position than idolaters, disagreed, so he should not grieve over his people's disagreement.
rows.anchor: وتسليته بأن أهل الكتاب وهم أحسن حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Torah disagreement included rejecting or hiding parts such as stoning, interpreting passages to suit desire, and inserting material as divine revelation.
rows.anchor: في تقرير بعضها وإبطال بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement involved only some people: corrupt editors were blameworthy, while those who opposed them were praiseworthy; the point warns against repeating it.
rows.anchor: بل كان للتحذير من الوقوع في مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using “differed in it” with fi treats the book figuratively as the domain or object of their disagreement and gathers its several forms.
rows.anchor: على الظرفية المجازية وهي كالملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is passive because the identity of the disputants is not the point; alternatively, the clause may attach to the preceding promise, with “between them” referring to those worshipped and God's prior wisdom delaying judgment.
rows.anchor: للمجهول إذ لا غرض إلا في ذكر الفعل لا في فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After consolation and reassurance, the Prophet is urged to persist in Islam's straight path and remain constant in its teachings.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن ذلك بالاستقامة لإفادة الدوام على العمل بتعاليم الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are included because deviation from scripture invites factions to alter it; upright practice of the complete law after faith prevents such disagreement.
rows.anchor: لأن الاعوجاج من دواعي الاختلاف في الكتاب بنهوض فرق من الأمة إلى تبديله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says earlier peoples were destroyed by excessive questioning and disagreement with their prophets; uprightness means carrying out the law without deviation.
rows.anchor: فإنما أهلك الذين من قبلكم كثرة مسائلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's direct address honors him as the first recipient; “as you were commanded” makes his straightness the model for the community.
rows.anchor: تنويها بشأنه ليبني عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison in “as commanded” is a circumstantial phrase equating uprightness with all other commands, effectively meaning “remain as you are.”
rows.anchor: يؤول هذا المعنى إلى أن تكون الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who repent with you” coordinates with the attached pronoun in “you were commanded”; the intervening prepositional phrase licenses the coordination.
rows.anchor: ومصحح العطف موجود وهو الفصل بالجار والمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who repent” are believers, since faith is repentance from associating partners; “with you” is circumstantial, not an attachment to repent.
rows.anchor: لأن الإيمان توبة من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be upright gathers the foundations and branches of religious rectitude.
rows.anchor: أصول الصلاح الديني وفروعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder for the Prophet; when companions noticed his gray hair, he said Hud and its sisters had made him gray, and when asked what in Hud he cited this command.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس : ما نزل على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not transgress” addresses the believers included in “those with you.”
rows.anchor: موجه إلى المؤمنين الذين صدق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgression originally means arrogance and audacity; here it means daring to violate commands, as in the warning to Israel.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا الجراءة على مخالفة ما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on transgression covers sources of wrongdoing; the next verse bars the remaining danger of being influenced by corrupt companions.
rows.anchor: فهو المنهي عنه بقوله بعد هذا

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says God placed religion between two prohibitions: do not transgress and do not incline toward wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: الحسن البصري : جعل الله الدين بين لاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's seeing warns against concealed transgression; “seeing” was chosen to convey clear and powerful knowledge of every deed.
rows.anchor: من بين بقية الأسماء الحسنى لدلالة مادته على العلم البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that good deeds remove sins explains the command to establish prayer; in context, “indeed” emphasizes the claim and signals its causal force.
rows.anchor: مسوقة مساق التعليل للأمر بإقامة الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing sins can mean good habits make sin easier to avoid, as prayer restrains indecency, or that good deeds erase guilt after a sin; both apply broadly.
rows.anchor: وإذهاب السيئات يشمل إذهاب وقوعها بأن يصير انسياق النفس إلى ترك السيئات سهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “sins” means minor sins, limited by verses that exempt minor lapses and promise their erasure when major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: ومحمل السيئات هنا على السيئات الصغائر التي هي من اللمم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Bukhari reports Ibn Masud's account of a man who illicitly kissed a woman and asked the Prophet about it; the verse was revealed, and the Prophet said it applies to anyone in his community who does such a deed.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه : أن رجلا أصاب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Tirmidhi reports Ibn Masud's account of a man who confessed intimate contact short of intercourse; the Prophet later recited the verse and said it applies to everyone, not only that man.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : جاء رجل

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Ibn Masud report hasan sahih; he also gives two reports, from Muadh and Abu al-Yusr, and calls those weak.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي : هذا حديث حسن صحيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada used the report's “it was revealed to him” wording to argue that this verse, unlike the rest of the surah, is Medinan.
rows.anchor: حمل ابن عباس وقتادة على القول بأن هذه الآية مدنية دون بقية هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If that wording is literal, the verse was inserted here because it fits the preceding command to be upright and the following command to be patient.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية ألحقت بهذه السورة في هذا المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who regard the whole surah as Meccan take the verse as a general command to pray, recited by the Prophet to a penitent; “revealed” can mean applying its general rule to his case.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين رجحوا أن السورة كلها مكية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In another Tirmidhi transmission through Alqama and al-Aswad, Ibn Masud says the Prophet recited the verse, without saying it was newly revealed.
rows.anchor: عن علقمة والأسود عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be patient continues the reassurance against delayed punishment for those who deny.
rows.anchor: سيقت مساق التثبيت من جراء تأخير عقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience follows uprightness and avoiding the wrongdoers because these commands are difficult and oppose many people's desires.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة وقوع الأمر بالصبر عقب الأمر بالاستقامة والنهي عن الركون إلى الذين ظلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is addressed as an honor, but the universal reason includes his community; patience is one of the good deeds of the righteous.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من العموم والتفريع المقتضي جمعهما أن الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is called a wage because it is promised as recompense for deeds and therefore resembles payment.
rows.anchor: وسمي الثواب أجرا لوقوعه جزاء على الأعمال وموعودا به فأشبه الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanatory resumption invites the reader to ask how Joseph received the chief wife's demand during an acute crisis.
rows.anchor: لأن ما حكي قبله مقام شدة من شأنه أن يسأل سامعه عن حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's words are a private prayer to God; he may instead have said them aloud to discourage the women.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه جهر به في ملئهن تأييسا لهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce al-sijn with kasra; Yaqub alone uses fatḥa, making it a verbal noun meaning imprisonment.
rows.anchor: يعقوب وحده بفتح السين على معنى المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph preferred prison's pain to unlawful pleasure because it would protect him from sin; his preference is genuine and arises from reflection.
rows.anchor: فلما علم أنه لا محيص من أحد الأمرين صار السجن محبوبا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying prison is dear is performative contentment with obeying God, not merely information about an inner state.
rows.anchor: فالإخبار بأن السجن أحب إليه من الاستمتاع بالمرأة مستعمل في إنشاء الرضى بالسجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative phrase about what they invite him to hints that social pressure usually makes compliance easier, yet the women's concerted demand did not break his resolve.
rows.anchor: لما في الصلة من الإيماء إلى كون المطلوب حالة هي مظنة الطواعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “they invite me” can mean women's collective desire generally or the gathered women who joined the chief wife's pressure; this parallels the plural in the later plot.
rows.anchor: فالواو الذي فيه هو حرف أصلي وليست واو الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's conditional statement expresses fear and dependence on God, disavowing his own power and fearing that his heart may turn toward forbidden pleasure; it functions as a prayer.
rows.anchor: فالخبر مستعمل في الدعاء ، ولذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣb means to incline toward something beloved; the ignorant are foolish and lack forbearance.
rows.anchor: أمل . والصبو : الميل إلى المحبوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Become one of the ignorant” is stronger than simply “be ignorant,” as with “one of the disgraced.”
rows.anchor: أكثر من أكن جاهلا كالقول في { وليكونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa indicates God's immediate answer; istajāba is more emphatic than ajāba.
rows.anchor: بفاء التعقيب إشارة إلى أن الله عجل إجابة دعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God diverted the effect of their plot by keeping Joseph steadfast and chaste when he was most vulnerable.
rows.anchor: وذلك بأن ثبته على العصمة فلم ينخدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Hearer, the Knower” explains the prompt answer: God answers quickly and knows pure inward intentions; hearing here means answering a request.
rows.anchor: أي أجاب دعاءه بدون مهلة لأنه سريع الإجابة وعليم بالضمائر الخالصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks a surprising later turn: after Joseph's innocence became clear, the authorities decided to imprison him.
rows.anchor: كما هو شأنها في عطف الجمل فإن ما بدا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chief wife feared gossip after the women dispersed, so she tried to cover Joseph's innocence by imprisoning him, making him appear guilty and perhaps returning him to her control.
rows.anchor: فرامت أن تغطي ذلك بسجن يوسف عليه السلام حتى يظهر في صورة المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Them” refers to the chief wife's group of advisers and commanders.
rows.anchor: لجماعة العزيز من مشير وآمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence with the oath lām is detached from “it appeared”; the omitted object can be inferred, showing suspension is not limited to verbs of thought, as Yunus ibn Habib held.
rows.anchor: جواب قسم محذوف ، وهي معلقة فعل

rows.speaker: يونس بن حبيب
rows.claim: Yunus ibn Habib held that suspension is caused by an element with sentence-initial force and need not be limited to verbs of thought.
rows.anchor: مذهب يونس بن حبيب ، لأن سبب التعليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians differed over whether a clause may serve as a subject: Hisham and Tha'lab allowed it generally, while al-Farra and others allowed it with a cognitive verb and suspension; this verse is cited as evidence, though suspension fits better.
rows.anchor: فأجازه هشام وثعلب مطلقا ، وأجازه الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Until a time” is indefinite; if spoken by the authorities, the term was open-ended, while if Qur'anic narration, its length is omitted because it is irrelevant to the story.
rows.anchor: فإن كان { حتى حين } من كلامهم كان المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs were proofs of Joseph's truth and the chief wife's falsehood.
rows.anchor: دلائل صدق يوسف عليه السلام وكذب امرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers use kasra in al-sijn here, meaning the place of confinement, because entering applies to a place, not the act of imprisonment.
rows.anchor: هنا بمعنى البيت الذي يسجن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two youths were the king's cupbearer and baker, imprisoned after the king became angry; an unnamed report says they were accused of poisoning his food and drink.
rows.anchor: وهذان الفتيان هما ساقي الملك وخبازه غضب عليهما الملك فأمر بسجنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation was a familiar Egyptian discipline, and God supported Joseph through it among the prisoners.
rows.anchor: وكان تعبير الرؤيا من فنون علمائهم فلذلك أيد الله به يوسف عليه السلام بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths inferred Joseph's intelligence and assumed he could interpret dreams without having seen proof; “excellent” may mean skilled in interpretation or understanding.
rows.anchor: أي المحسنين التعبير ، أو المحسنين الفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan here means precision or proficiency, as in saying someone does not “do reading well.”
rows.anchor: هو لا يحسن القراءة ، أي لا يتقنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prisoners commonly exchanged dreams because they lacked news and conversation, and they hoped dreams would foretell escape.
rows.anchor: لفقدانهم الأخبار التي هي وسائل المحادثة والمحاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king's later request shows that Egyptian courtiers included people thought capable of interpreting dreams.
rows.anchor: دل عليه قوله تعالى حكاية عن ملك مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣr means squeezing a moist substance to extract liquid; ʿaṣīr names the extracted liquid after its source.
rows.anchor: الضغط باليد أو بحجر أو نحوه على شيء فيه رطوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bread is a baked portion of flour and water, also called a loaf; “its interpretation” refers either to the mentioned matter or to the dream as a class.
rows.anchor: اسم لقطعة من دقيق البر أو الشعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's vocative stresses the importance of his interpretation and addresses them as fellow prisoners.
rows.anchor: افتتح خطابهما بالنداء اهتماما بما يلقيه إليهما من التعبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Joseph spoke in the order shown, he gave both interpretations together in a veiled summary so the condemned man could work out his fate gradually.
rows.anchor: في عبارة واحدة مجملة ، لأن في تأويل إحدى الرؤيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse may condense Joseph's original speech, in which he directly assigned each interpretation to one man.
rows.anchor: كان في الآية إيجاز لحكاية كلام يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The matter is decided” confirms the interpretation because their urgent question concerned what would happen to them in prison.
rows.anchor: تحقيق لما دلت عليه الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiftāʾ is asking for a fatwa: an explanation that resolves difficulty or uncertainty; the verb aftā retains its hamza and is linked by some to fatā, youth, because clear explanation strengthens the recipient.
rows.anchor: الإخبار بإزالة مشكل ، أو إرشاد إلى إزالة حيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man Joseph expected to survive was the cupbearer; “thought” here approaches certainty because Joseph trusted his interpretation.
rows.anchor: والظن هنا مستعمل في القريب من القطع لأنه لا يشك في صحة تعبيره الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks the cupbearer to tell his master, the king of Egypt, about Joseph's case and injustice.
rows.anchor: مظلمته ، أي اذكرني لربك ، أي سيدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in “Satan made him forget” may refer to the cupbearer: he forgot Joseph and the king; or to Joseph: Satan made Joseph forget God, a different remembrance.
rows.anchor: أي أنسى الشيطان الذي نجا أن يذكره لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings may be intended: Joseph forgot to ask God for deliverance, which caused the cupbearer to forget him; this becomes divine reproach for relying on people.
rows.anchor: ولعل كلا الاحتمالين مراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This double reading tactfully reports the lapse, since an allusive statement is gentler than a direct one.
rows.anchor: لأن الكلام الموجه في المعاني الموجهة ألطف من الصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍʿ means a number from three to nine.
rows.anchor: البضع : من الثلاث إلى التسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account implies the prison had no reliable register, oversight, or periodic report to the king; Islamic law addressed this neglect by requiring a judge to review prisoners daily.
rows.anchor: وهذا من الإهمال والتهاون بحقوق الناس وقد أبطله الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven ears are joined to the seven cows; the wording recalls the parable of a grain producing seven ears.
rows.anchor: و { وسبع سنبلات } معطوف على { سبع بقرات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ means the leading or distinguished people.
rows.anchor: الملأ : أعيان الناس . وتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iftāʾ is giving a fatwa or explanation, as discussed in the earlier prison scene.
rows.anchor: الإخبار بالفتوى . وتقدمت آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fi figuratively marks an interpretation attached to the dream, like an explanation attached to something concise.
rows.anchor: للظرفية المجازية التي هي بمعنى الملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting “for the dream” before its verb observes the cadence and foregrounds the dream; its definite article is generic.
rows.anchor: للرعاية على الفاصلة مع الاهتمام بالرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām reinforces the delayed verb's connection to its object; al-Zamakhshari says careful scholars prefer the light form ʿabara, not the doubled form.
rows.anchor: لام التقوية لضعف العامل عن العمل بالتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur cites a verse recited by al-Mubarrad from an unnamed Bedouin as evidence for dream-interpreter wording: “I saw my dream, then interpreted it; I was an interpreter of dreams.”
rows.anchor: على بيت أنشده المبرد في كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation was a practiced Egyptian science with priestly rules; both the prisoners' request and the king's consultation indicate that the court included interpreters.
rows.anchor: وكان الكهنة منهم يعدونه من علومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah says Pharaoh summoned Egyptian magicians and sages but found no interpreter; dream interpretation was associated with priests because it concerned the unseen.
rows.anchor: جميع سحرة مصر وجميع حكمائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic biography reports that Kisra sent for the soothsayer Satiḥ to interpret a dream around the Prophet's birth, counted among prophetic portents; Kisra was alarmed and sent Abd al-Masih.
rows.anchor: أن كسرى أرسل إلى سطيح الكاهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the dream” refers back to this particular dream, after the earlier generic use.
rows.anchor: تعريف العهد ، والمعهود الرؤيا التي كان يقصها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adghāth is the plural of a bundle of mixed plants; the dream is likened to tangled fragments that resist interpretation.
rows.anchor: جمع ضغث بكسر الضاد المعجمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahlām is plural because the king's single dream contained several images.
rows.anchor: باعتبار تعدد الأشياء المرئية في ذلك الحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ba in “in interpreting dreams” strengthens the verb's attachment to its object, like the ba in “wipe your heads,” because the courtiers deny competence.
rows.anchor: لتأكيد اتصال العامل بالمفعول ، وهي من قبيل باء الإلصاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the courtiers could not interpret the dream, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and offered to explain it.
rows.anchor: فلما ظهر عوص تعبير هذا الحلم تذكر ساقي الملك ما جرى له مع يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Starting with “I” and making himself the subject attracts the king's surprise and strengthens the claim that he can explain a baffling dream.
rows.anchor: وابتداء كلامه بضميره وجعله مسندا إليه وخبره فعلي لقصد استجلاب تعجب الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling himself the one who will inform them is figurative because he is the cause of the explanation; “send me” seeks the king's permission to leave his presence.
rows.anchor: مجاز عقلي لأنه سبب الإنباء ، ولذلك قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His confidence that Joseph remained in prison suggests it was a private prison: any release or death would have reached the king and his court.
rows.anchor: ولعل سبب يقينه ببقاء يوسف عليه السلام في السجن أنه كان سجن الخاصة
